html:
Tyrian purple was a deep red-purple dye made from sea snails, the murex, in the Phoenician cities of the Lebanese coast, above all Tyre and Sidon. Its making goes back to the Bronze Age.

Thousands of snails were crushed and left to rot in vats to make a little dye, so it was hugely expensive, and the works stank. Heaps of crushed shells still lie near the old towns. Cloth dyed with it held its colour for years.

The dye was one of the luxury goods that made the Phoenicians rich, and the Greek name Phoenicia may come from a word for this red. In Rome purple marked rank, and later only the emperor could wear robes of it, a custom kept in Constantinople. See also Alexander's siege of Tyre.
sum: Tyrian purple was a deep red-purple dye made from sea snails, the murex, in the Phoenician cities of the Lebanese coast, above all Tyre and Sidon. Its making goes back to the Bronze Age.
